[pyprland]
plugins = [
    "scratchpads",
]

# Only the scratchpads plugin is enabled — no other pyprland feature
# (expose, magnify, monitors, wallpapers, etc.) is loaded or active.

# VSCode uses Electron's single-instance lock: if one is already running,
# a second `code` launch just hands off to it and exits immediately. That
# confuses pyprland's default PID-based process tracking (it looks like the
# launch "failed") — process_tracking=false is required here.
#
# match_by="class" was tried and REJECTED: verified live that it makes
# pyprland install a class-scoped window rule that auto-routes ANY new
# `code` window (not just the scratchpad one) into the hidden special
# workspace — including windows you open normally. That's the exact bug
# that broke VSCode earlier in this config's history. Instead: a dedicated,
# always-empty folder (~/.vscode-scratch) gives every scratchpad launch a
# stable, unique window title ("<folder> - Visual Studio Code") that stays
# constant regardless of which file is focused inside it — verified live,
# confirmed it never matches a normal VSCode window opened on any other
# folder.
[scratchpads.code]
command = "code --new-window /home/krubics/.vscode-scratch"
class = "code"
match_by = "title"
title = "re:.*vscode-scratch.*"
process_tracking = false
size = "80% 85%"
lazy = true

# Dedicated scratchpad terminal using kitty, NOT your default ghostty.
# Ghostty's `class` config only affects X11 WM_CLASS ("no effect otherwise"
# per its own docs) — confirmed empirically, it cannot get a distinguishable
# Wayland app_id. kitty supports a real --class override (the pattern the
# official pyprland docs use), so it's the reliable choice for a scratchpad
# that must be told apart from ordinary terminal windows. Your SUPER+RETURN
# ghostty terminal is completely unaffected.
# match_by="class"/process_tracking=false here too: pyprland's default
# spawn-wait timeout is shorter than this system's kitty startup latency,
# so it gives up waiting even though the window reliably appears a moment
# later. `kitty-scratch-term` is a unique class (nothing else uses it), so
# class-based matching carries zero ambiguity risk.
[scratchpads.term]
command = "kitty --class kitty-scratch-term"
class = "kitty-scratch-term"
match_by = "class"
process_tracking = false
animation = "fromTop"
size = "75% 60%"
margin = 50
lazy = true

# Zen shares class="zen" across every window regardless of profile, so
# class-based matching can't distinguish this scratchpad instance from your
# regular Zen windows (verified: match_by="class" does a blind scan of all
# current windows, not a spawn-correlated one — unsafe here). The wrapper
# forces a fixed marker page title instead, which title-matching can key on
# without ambiguity. process_tracking stays off because Zen's cold start
# (fresh isolated profile) can exceed pyprland's internal spawn-wait window;
# title matching keeps working via event-driven re-matching regardless.
[scratchpads.browser]
command = "/home/krubics/.config/hypr/scripts/zen-scratch.sh"
class = "zen"
match_by = "title"
title = "re:.*zen-scratch-marker.*"
process_tracking = false
size = "85% 85%"

-- ============================================================
--  keybinds.lua  —  Omarchy's keymap, ported to Hyprland 0.55+ Lua
--
--  Grammar (Omarchy's, kept faithfully):
--    SUPER            = window & workspace management
--    SUPER + SHIFT    = launch apps  (and "relocate" on numbers/arrows)
--    SUPER + CTRL     = system / settings
--    SUPER + ALT      = a variant of the base action
--    CTRL + ALT       = session-level
--
--  Pruned to your setup: only terminal / browser / files / Obsidian
--  apps; Omarchy's own menu scripts swapped for standard Linux tools.
--
--  NOTE on hl.dsp.exec_raw("..."): several Omarchy actions use
--  dispatchers the typed Lua API hasn't wrapped yet (swapwindow,
--  movetoworkspacesilent, togglesplit, pin, centerwindow). exec_raw
--  runs the old-style dispatcher string verbatim — it's the bridge
--  for anything not yet in hl.dsp.*. If your build names it
--  differently, the error will point right at these lines.
--
--  Pull in from hyprland.lua with:  require("keybinds")
-- ============================================================

-- ---- Edit these to match your machine -----------------------
local vars = require("conf.vars")
local modKey = "SUPER"

-- ============================================================
--  APPLICATIONS  (SUPER + SHIFT = launch)
-- ============================================================
hl.bind(modKey .. " + RETURN",         hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.terminal))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + SPACE",          hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.launcher))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + B",      hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.browser))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + F",          hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.yazi))   -- yazi (terminal FM)
hl.bind(modKey .. " + CTRL + SHIFT + F",  hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.files))  -- nautilus (moved off SUPER+SHIFT+F for herdr search)
hl.bind(modKey .. " + O",      hl.dsp.exec_cmd(vars.obsidian))
hl.bind(modKey .. " + A",      function()
  hl.exec_cmd(vars.browser)
  hl.exec_cmd(vars.terminal)
end)

---- Scroll -------------------------------------------------------
-- hl.bind("ALT + semicolon", hl.dsp.scroll({ direction = "down" }))
hl.bind("ALT + P", function() 
  hl.exec_cmd("move +col")
end)

-- ============================================================
--  WINDOW MANAGEMENT  (SUPER)
-- ============================================================
hl.bind(modKey .. " + Q", hl.dsp.window.close())                     -- close window
hl.bind(modKey .. " + D", hl.dsp.window.float({ action = "toggle" })) -- toggle float
hl.bind(modKey .. " + J", hl.dsp.exec_raw("togglesplit"))            -- flip split axis
hl.bind(modKey .. " + bracketright", hl.dsp.window.fullscreen({ mode = 0 }))    -- fullscreen
hl.bind(modKey .. " + GRAVE", hl.dsp.layout("rotatesplit 90"))

  hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.exec_raw("centerwindow"))

arguments.content:
[pyprland]
plugins = [
    "scratchpads",
]

# Only the scratchpads plugin is enabled — no other pyprland feature
# (expose, magnify, monitors, wallpapers, etc.) is loaded or active.

# VSCode uses Electron's single-instance lock: if one is already running,
# a second `code` launch just hands off to it and exits immediately. That
# confuses pyprland's default PID-based process tracking (it looks like the
# launch "failed") — process_tracking=false is required here.
#
# match_by="class" was tried and REJECTED: verified live that it makes
# pyprland install a class-scoped window rule that auto-routes ANY new
# `code` window (not just the scratchpad one) into the hidden special
# workspace — including windows you open normally. That's the exact bug
# that broke VSCode earlier in this config's history. Instead: a dedicated,
# always-empty folder (~/.vscode-scratch) gives every scratchpad launch a
# stable, unique window title ("<folder> - Visual Studio Code") that stays
# constant regardless of which file is focused inside it — verified live,
# confirmed it never matches a normal VSCode window opened on any other
# folder.
[scratchpads.code]
command = "code --new-window /home/krubics/.vscode-scratch"
class = "code"
match_by = "title"
title = "re:.*vscode-scratch.*"
process_tracking = false
size = "80% 85%"
lazy = true

# Dedicated scratchpad terminal using ghostty, NOT your default SUPER+RETURN
# ghostty. Ghostty's `class` config sets the GTK application id (which is
# also the Wayland app_id), and per its own docs "changing this value
# between invocations will create new, separate instances" — so passing a
# unique --class here spawns a genuinely separate ghostty instance rather
# than opening a new window in your regular one. `com.krubics.ghostty-scratch`
# is a unique app id (nothing else uses it), so class-based matching carries
# zero ambiguity risk. process_tracking stays off for the same reason as the
# other scratchpads below: keeps matching purely event-driven instead of
# racing pyprland's internal spawn-wait timeout.
[scratchpads.term]
command = "ghostty --class=com.krubics.ghostty-scratch"
class = "com.krubics.ghostty-scratch"
match_by = "class"
process_tracking = false
animation = "fromTop"
size = "75% 60%"
margin = 50
lazy = true

# Zen shares class="zen" across every window regardless of profile, so
# class-based matching can't distinguish this scratchpad instance from your
# regular Zen windows (verified: match_by="class" does a blind scan of all
# current windows, not a spawn-correlated one — unsafe here). The wrapper
# opens a fixed marker page (data: URL) whose title includes
# "zen-scratch-marker", which title-matching keys on without ambiguity.
# process_tracking stays off because Zen's cold start (fresh isolated
# profile) can exceed pyprland's internal spawn-wait window; title matching
# keeps working via event-driven re-matching regardless.
[scratchpads.browser]
command = "/home/krubics/.config/hypr/scripts/zen-scratch.sh"
class = "zen"
match_by = "title"
title = "re:.*zen-scratch-marker.*"
process_tracking = false
size = "85% 85%"
lazy = true

#!/bin/sh
# Scratchpad Zen browser — isolated profile, forced new instance, so it's a
# genuinely separate process pyprland can track by PID (safe: no shared
# class="zen" ambiguity with your regular Zen windows). First-ever launch
# creates the profile (~1-13s depending on system load); every launch after
# is fast (~1s) since the profile already exists.
#
# The data: URL below sets the *page* title to "zen-scratch-marker", which
# Zen folds into the OS window title. pyprland's [scratchpads.browser] in
# ~/.config/pypr/config.toml matches on that title regex — without this,
# there is nothing distinguishing this window from a normal Zen window and
# toggling would never find/hide it.
mkdir -p "$HOME/.zen-scratch"
exec zen --new-instance --profile "$HOME/.zen-scratch" \
    "data:text/html,<title>zen-scratch-marker</title>"

arguments.content:
#!/bin/sh
# Scratchpad Zen browser — isolated profile, forced new instance, so it's a
# genuinely separate process pyprland can track by PID (safe: no shared
# class="zen" ambiguity with your regular Zen windows). First-ever launch
# creates the profile (~1-13s depending on system load); every launch after
# is fast (~1s) since the profile already exists.
#
# The local HTML file below sets the *page* title to "zen-scratch-marker",
# which Zen folds into the OS window title. pyprland's [scratchpads.browser]
# in ~/.config/pypr/config.toml matches on that title regex — without this,
# there is nothing distinguishing this window from a normal Zen window and
# toggling would never find/hide it.
#
# A data: URL was tried and REJECTED: verified live that Firefox-based
# browsers (Zen included) silently refuse to navigate to a data: URL passed
# as a command-line argument (security restriction), so the window title
# stayed the generic "Zen Browser" and title-matching never fired. A real
# file:// URL has no such restriction.
MARKER_PAGE="$HOME/.config/hypr/scripts/zen-scratch-marker.html"
mkdir -p "$HOME/.zen-scratch"
exec zen --new-instance --profile "$HOME/.zen-scratch" "file://$MARKER_PAGE"

    """Align to left edge with margin."""

    """Align to right edge with margin."""
    return mon_w - client_w - margin_w + mon_x

    """Align to top edge with margin."""
    return margin_h + mon_y

    """Align to bottom edge with margin."""
    return mon_h - client_h - margin_h + mon_y

There's no dedicated kill command for scratchpad apps through pypr itself—closing them relies on the app's own mechanisms like Ctrl+Q or using standard window close binds when they're visible. If a scratchpad is hidden in a special workspace, you'd need to toggle it visible first before you can close it normally.

Alternatively, I could use a hyprctl dispatch command to close the window by class selector regardless of which workspace it's on, since special workspace windows are still valid targets for dispatch commands. There's also a `close_on_hide` config option that automatically closes the window on hide instead of just hiding it, but that would defeat the lazy persistence benefit since it would respawn the app on every toggle. Let me verify the exact hyprctl syntax for closing windows by class selector.

def translate_dispatcher(name: str, arg: str, *, is_mouse: bool = False) -> str | None:
    """Translate ``(dispatcher_name, arg)`` to a Lua ``hl.dsp.*`` call.

    Returns ``None`` when we don't know how to render the dispatcher.
    Shared by the bind emitter (config-side) and ``dispatch_to_lua``
    (runtime live-apply side) so both produce the same translation.
    """
    if name == "exec":
        # Lua-mode Hyprland rejects the ``keyword`` IPC verb at config-eval
        # time, so a whole-arg ``hyprctl keyword …`` has to become native Lua.
        # A whole-arg ``hyprctl dispatch …`` can also collapse to a native
        # dispatcher, sparing the shell hop. Anything else (a larger shell
        # command) passes through verbatim:
        #   1. Whole arg is ``hyprctl keyword …`` → inline ``hl.config`` closure.
        #   2. Whole arg is ``hyprctl dispatch VERB ARGS`` → native dispatcher.
        #   3. Otherwise → leave the shell string untouched. ``hyprctl dispatch``
        #      embedded in a larger shell command is a runtime IPC call to the
        #      ``hyprctl`` binary; it behaves identically regardless of config
        #      language, so rewriting it to Lua syntax would only break it.
        keyword = parse_hyprctl_keyword(arg)
        if keyword is not None:
            return emit_keyword_setter_closure(*keyword)
        dispatch = parse_hyprctl_dispatch(arg)
        if dispatch is not None:
            translation = translate_dispatcher(dispatch[0], dispatch[1])
            if translation is not None:
                return translation
        return f"hl.dsp.exec_cmd({quote_string(arg)})"
    handler = _DISPATCHERS.get(name)
    if handler is None:
        return None
    return handler(arg, is_mouse)


def dispatcher_drops_address_selector(name: str, arg: str) -> bool:
    """Detect an ``address:`` selector the dispatcher's Lua emitter would drop."""
    if name in _ADDRESS_AWARE:
        return False
    return arg.startswith("address:") or ",address:" in arg

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Direction -> (x_strategy, y_strategy) mapping
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_PosFn = Callable[[int, int, int, int], int]

_DIRECTION_MAP: dict[str, tuple[_PosFn, _PosFn]] = {
    "fromtop": (_x_center, _y_top),
    "frombottom": (_x_center, _y_bottom),
    "fromleft": (_x_left, _y_center),
    "fromright": (_x_right, _y_center),
    "fromtopleft": (_x_left, _y_top),
    "fromtopright": (_x_right, _y_top),
    "frombottomleft": (_x_left, _y_bottom),
    "frombottomright": (_x_right, _y_bottom),
}


class Placement:
    """Compute on-screen and off-screen window positions for each animation direction."""

    @staticmethod
    def get(animation_type: str, monitor: MonitorInfo, client: ClientInfo, margin: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Get destination coordinate for the provided animation type.

        Args:
            animation_type: Type of animation (fromtop, frombottom, etc.)
            monitor: Monitor information
            client: Client window information
            margin: Margin to apply
        """
        x_fn, y_fn = _DIRECTION_MAP[animation_type]
        mon_x, mon_y = monitor["x"], monitor["y"]
        mon_w, mon_h = get_size(monitor)
        client_w, client_h = client["size"]
        margin_w = convert_monitor_dimension(margin, mon_w, monitor)
        margin_h = convert_monitor_dimension(margin, mon_h, monitor)
        return (
            x_fn(mon_x, mon_w, client_w, margin_w),
            y_fn(mon_y, mon_h, client_h, margin_h),
        )

    @staticmethod
    def get_offscreen(animation_type: str, monitor: MonitorInfo, client: ClientInfo, margin: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
        """Get off-screen position for the given animation type.

        Computes the final on-screen position via ``get()``, then pushes the
        window far off-screen along the animation axis.  An extra monitor
        dimension is subtracted/added so the window doesn't appear on an
        adjacent monitor in multi-monitor setups.

        For each axis the direction operates on (left/right or top/bottom),
        the coordinate is pushed far offscreen.  For the centered axis
        (if any), the on-screen coordinate is preserved.

        Args:
            animation_type: Type of animation (fromtop, frombottom, etc.)
            monitor: Monitor information
            client: Client window information
            margin: Margin to apply
        """
        fx, fy = Placement.get(animation_type, monitor, client, margin)
        mon_x, mon_y = monitor["x"], monitor["y"]
        mon_w, mon_h = get_size(monitor)
        client_w, client_h = client["size"]

        x_fn, y_fn = _DIRECTION_MAP[animation_type]

        # For each axis: push far offscreen if direction uses that edge, otherwise keep on-screen position
        if x_fn is _x_left:
            off_x = mon_x - client_w - mon_w
        elif x_fn is _x_right:
            off_x = mon_x + mon_w + mon_w
        else:
            off_x = fx

        if y_fn is _y_top:
            off_y = mon_y - client_h - mon_h
        elif y_fn is _y_bottom:
            off_y = mon_y + mon_h + mon_h
        else:
            off_y = fy

        return (off_x, off_y)

"""Conversion functions for units used in Pyprland & plugins."""

from typing import Literal

from ..common import is_rotated
from ..models import MonitorInfo

MonitorDimension = Literal["width", "height"]


def convert_monitor_dimension(size: int | str, ref_value: int, monitor: MonitorInfo) -> int:
    """Convert `size` into pixels (given a reference value applied to a `monitor`).

    if size is an integer, assumed pixels & return it
    if size is a string, expects a "%" or "px" suffix
    else throws an error

    Args:
        size: The size to convert (int or string with unit)
        ref_value: Reference value for percentage calculations
        monitor: Monitor information
    """
    if isinstance(size, int):
        return size

    if isinstance(size, str):
        if size.endswith("%"):
            p = int(size[:-1])
            return int(ref_value / monitor["scale"] * p / 100)
        if size.endswith("px"):
            return int(size[:-2])

    msg = f"Unsupported format: {size} (applied to {ref_value})"
    raise ValueError(msg)


def convert_coords(coords: str, monitor: MonitorInfo) -> list[int]:
    """Convert a string like "X Y" to coordinates relative to monitor.

    Supported formats for X, Y:
    - Percentage: "V%". V in [0; 100]
    - Pixels: "Vpx". V should fit in your screen and not be zero

    Example:
    "10% 20%", monitor 800x600 => 80, 120

    Args:
        coords: Coordinates string "X Y"
        monitor: Monitor information
    """
    coord_list = [coord.strip() for coord in coords.split()]
    refs: tuple[MonitorDimension, MonitorDimension] = ("height", "width") if is_rotated(monitor) else ("width", "height")
    return [convert_monitor_dimension(name, monitor[ref], monitor) for (name, ref) in zip(coord_list, refs, strict=False)]

So the `position` parameter uses the window's top-left corner as the reference point, not its center — meaning `position = "50% 50%"` would place the top-left at screen center, not center the window itself. To actually center it, I'd need to calculate the offset based on the window's dimensions, which is tricky when the size is defined as a percentage rather than fixed pixels.

For a window sized at 80% × 85% of the monitor, the top-left corner should sit at 10% and 7.5% respectively to achieve true centering. But looking at the available animation directions, there's no built-in "fromCenter" option — only the cardinal and diagonal directions, plus empty string for no animation. So to get full 2D centering, I'd either disable animation entirely and use computed position values, or accept that any slide-in animation will only center along one axis.

The real constraint is that `position` and animation are mutually exclusive in the code — setting a position value disables the slide animation completely. So I can't have both a fromTop slide-in effect AND exact both-axis centering simultaneously. The trade-off is either static centered placement with no animation, or keep the animation and accept that only one axis gets centered by design.

Looking at the actual config setup, the default animation is already "fromTop" for code and browser configs (since animation isn't explicitly set, it defaults to fromTop), which means they're already horizontally centered. To also center vertically, I'd need to either drop the animation entirely and use an explicit position, or use a fixed margin value — but a fixed margin won't give true centering since it's a static distance from the top edge rather than a dynamic calculation based on window height.

command = "code --new-window /home/krubics/.vscode-scratch"
class = "code"
match_by = "title"

[pyprland]
plugins = [
    "scratchpads",
]

# Only the scratchpads plugin is enabled — no other pyprland feature
# (expose, magnify, monitors, wallpapers, etc.) is loaded or active.

# VSCode uses Electron's single-instance lock: if one is already running,
# a second `code` launch just hands off to it and exits immediately. That
# confuses pyprland's default PID-based process tracking (it looks like the
# launch "failed") — process_tracking=false is required here.
#
# match_by="class" was tried and REJECTED: verified live that it makes
# pyprland install a class-scoped window rule that auto-routes ANY new
# `code` window (not just the scratchpad one) into the hidden special
# workspace — including windows you open normally. That's the exact bug
# that broke VSCode earlier in this config's history. Instead: a dedicated,
# always-empty folder (~/.vscode-scratch) gives every scratchpad launch a
# stable, unique window title ("<folder> - Visual Studio Code") that stays
# constant regardless of which file is focused inside it — verified live,
# confirmed it never matches a normal VSCode window opened on any other
# folder.
[scratchpads.code]
command = "code --new-window /home/krubics/.vscode-scratch"
class = "code"
match_by = "title"
title = "re:.*vscode-scratch.*"
process_tracking = false
size = "80% 85%"
# Explicit center override: with size 80%x85%, the top-left corner sits at
# ((100-80)/2, (100-85)/2) so the window lands dead-center regardless of
# monitor resolution. `animation` (default "fromTop") still plays — it only
# controls the off-screen starting point, the position always wins for the
# resting spot (see pyprland's transitions.py: _fix_position runs after the
# slide and is re-applied on a settle tick).
position = "10% 7.5%"
lazy = true

# also the Wayland app_id), and per its own docs "changing this value
# between invocations will create new, separate instances" — so passing a
# unique --class here spawns a genuinely separate ghostty instance rather
# than opening a new window in your regular one. `com.krubics.ghostty-scratch`
# is a unique app id (nothing else uses it), so class-based matching carries
# zero ambiguity risk. process_tracking stays off for the same reason as the
# other scratchpads below: keeps matching purely event-driven instead of
# racing pyprland's internal spawn-wait timeout.
[scratchpads.term]
command = "ghostty --class=com.krubics.ghostty-scratch"
class = "com.krubics.ghostty-scratch"
match_by = "class"
process_tracking = false
animation = "fromTop"
size = "75% 60%"

grep -n "\.local/bin\|PATH" /home/krubics/.zshrc /home/krubics/.bashrc /home/krubics/.profile /home/krubics/.zprofile 2>/dev/null
echo "=== which shell ==="
getent passwd krubics | cut -d: -f7
echo "=== pypr binary ==="
ls -la /home/krubics/.local/bin/pypr
head -1 /home/krubics/.local/bin/pypr
echo "=== how was it installed ==="
pip show pyprland 2>&1 | head -5
pipx list 2>&1 | grep -i pypr
which pip3
python3 -m pip show pyprland 2>&1 | head -5
